# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec (when written): `SPEC.md`.

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to `BACKLOG.md` as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs or issues.
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission". Reasoning effort per role is set in `SPEC.md`.
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>

63→approved spec; the mission creates `mission/observatory-v1` from it):
64→
65→```sh
66→droid exec --mission --auto high \
67→  --model claude-fable-5.1          --reasoning-effort high \
68→  --worker-model claude-sonnet-5-5  --worker-reasoning-effort medium \
69→  --validator-model claude-opus-5-5 --validator-reasoning-effort high \
70→  --output-format text \
71→  -f SPEC.md
72→```

74→| Flag | Value | Reason |
75→|---|---|---|
76→| `--mission --auto high` | required | Missions auto-approve proposals and need `--auto high` (Droid 0.247.0 `droid exec --help`). The hooks in `.factory/hooks.json` are the guard, not the prompt. |
77→| `--model` | `claude-fable-5.1` | Orchestrator (D-006, corrected 2026-10-22 from the misspelt `claude-fable-5-1`, which fell back to GPT-6 Sol). Factory catalog id, 4× multiplier. |
78→| `--reasoning-effort` | `high` | Fable's default; planning and integration are where judgment is bought. `xhigh`/`max` on a 4× model is not justified before a measured need. |
79→| `--worker-model` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | Workers (D-006). 0.8× multiplier. |
80→| `--worker-reasoning-effort` | `medium` | Workers build bounded features against tests already written as the contract; one step below the model default to make the cost/quality split measurable in lane 9. Raised to `high` for the UI milestones if the M1 go/no-go shows UI rework above the threshold (decision file). |
81→| `--validator-model` | `claude-opus-5-5` | Validators, scrutiny and user testing (D-006). 1.6× multiplier. |
82→| `--validator-reasoning-effort` | `high` | Above Opus's default `medium`: validation is where correctness is bought (D-006 alternatives). |
83→| `--output-format` | `text` | The terminal is for the human; the dataset is the session JSONL under `~/.factory/sessions/`, which attach and replay read. |
84→| `-f SPEC.md` | this file | The mission plans from the approved spec (template, last paragraph). |

88→`missionModelSettings.workerModel`, `.workerReasoningEffort`, `.validationWorkerModel`,
89→`.validationWorkerReasoningEffort`. The three reasoning-effort keys are added with the spec PR

92→**Mission branch.** `mission/observatory-v1`, created from `main` at the commit that contains this
93→approved spec. One pull request `mission/observatory-v1` → `main` at the end of the mission, opened
94→by the orchestrator, merged by the human after `gate` is green. Nothing else reaches `main`
95→(rule 12). The branch is deleted at the merge (PRD §2).

97→**Worktree policy.** One worktree per milestone: `git worktree add ../observatory-wt/<m> -b wt/<m>
98→mission/observatory-v1` where `<m>` is `s`, `m0` … `m5`. Workers and validators of a milestone
99→work only inside its worktree. Two worktrees never edit the same file (rule 13); the shared files
100→(`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `docs/decisions/README.md`, `reports/`) are written by
101→the orchestrator on the mission branch at integration. Integration is `git merge --no-ff wt/<m>`
102→into `mission/observatory-v1` by the orchestrator, then `make check` locally, then the
103→`mission-checks` run on the push must be green before the next milestone starts. A worktree is
104→removed after integration; its branch stays (history).
105→
106→**Gate command.** `make check` is the only local gate: it is exactly what `mission-branch.yml`
107→runs (rule 5). A worker hands off only with `make check` green in its worktree; the orchestrator
108→integrates only with `make check` green on the mission branch.
109→
110→**Hooks that must be active.** `.factory/hooks.json`: `guard-git.sh` (PreToolUse on `Execute`,
111→blocks amend/reset/rebase/stash/force-push/push-to-main) and `log-tool-call.sh` (PostToolUse,
112→appends one JSON line per tool call to `build-log/<UTC-day>/<session>.jsonl`). Git hooks via
113→`make hooks` (`core.hooksPath=.githooks`): `pre-commit` (gitleaks on staged files, file size, debt
114→markers, decisions index, rustfmt, markdownlint), `commit-msg` (subject ≤ 72 chars, no WIP/fixup),
115→`pre-push` (no `main`, no non-fast-forward). A worker that finds a hook missing stops and reports;
116→it never disables or bypasses one (`--no-verify` is a rule 12 violation).
117→
118→**Usage budget per milestone.** Unit: USD-equivalent at `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`, computed
119→from the token counts Factory reports for the mission's sessions (the usage page or the stream's
120→`usage.reported`), pasted into `reports/usage/<milestone>.md` at integration (rule 7). Factory
121→Standard Credits are recorded next to it when visible. The caps below are the owner's planning
122→numbers, not measurements; this is the first mission and there is no prior run to calibrate on.
123→
124→| Milestone | Cap (USD-eq) | Reason for the size |
125→|---|---|---|
126→| S  walking skeleton | 40 | Thin slice, few files, mostly scaffolding and one fixture. |
127→| M0 capture and mapping | 60 | Mapper plus golden tests; the capture already exists (§3 M0). |
128→| M1 board, replay, attach | 150 | Largest UI milestone and the Leptos go/no-go; rework budget inside. |
129→| M2 host | 80 | RPC adapter plus launch screen; the control channel is new ground. |
130→| M3 intervention | 60 | Lane-7 semantics over M2 controls; small surface. |
131→| M4 branch, gate, fix loop | 120 | Two adapters (git, GitHub), the demo branch pair, a live PR loop. |
132→| M5 time, waste, cost | 120 | The metric engine and its oracle test; export; charts. |
133→| Total | 630 | Hard stop for the mission; the final PR and fixes come out of the unspent remainder. |

135→At a cap the orchestrator stops dispatching, writes the usage so far to `reports/usage/`, raises
136→the stall flag and waits for the human (rule 15). Spending beyond a cap is a deviation (rule 9).

138→**What the human will answer mid-mission.** Only at a milestone boundary or when the stall flag is
139→up (rule 15): the M1 go/no-go (PRD §12), a budget cap reached, a proposed deviation from this spec
140→with its reason and cost, a keychain item or GitHub permission the mission cannot create itself
141→(§3 M4, §5.9), the reference spreadsheet for M5 (B-008), and a red `gate` on the final PR.

147→## 3. Milestones
148→
149→Seven milestones on the board of the build: the walking skeleton `S` first (rule 2), then
150→`M0`–`M5` in PRD §13 order. A milestone is integrated into the mission branch, never shipped. The
151→spec itself is not a milestone: it is approved before the mission starts.
152→
153→**B-010 settled: skeleton before M0, and the capture is this mission.** Rule 2 wants the thinnest
154→end-to-end slice first; PRD §13 wants M0 to freeze the mapping before M1–M5 are planned in detail.
155→Both hold because the capture needs no extra mission: the moment the owner runs the §2 command, the
156→orchestrator's session JSONL is growing under `~/.factory/sessions/`, and the skeleton's workers
157→and validators add child sessions for every role. `S` replays a snapshot of that file through a
158→mapper that knows nothing yet (every line is `unknown.event`, counted). `M0` snapshots the same
159→sessions again at `S` integration, now with all four roles present, freezes it as the fixture,
160→and drives the unknown count to zero. The optional B-009 pre-capture is not needed; a small
161→sample-repo mission (PRD §13 M0) is the fallback only if role identification cannot be established
162→from this mission's own files.

166→- Tests first (rule 1): each feature begins with a red test committed in the worktree; the
167→  scrutiny validator checks that the red run exists in the worker's log.

170→  on the push, zero blocking findings open, §9/§10 rows written, README/BACKLOG/decisions index
171→  updated (rule 16), `reports/usage/<m>.md` and `reports/readiness/<date>-<m>.json` added
172→  (B-015), and no `unknown.event` on the capture if the milestone adds a source (rule 18).
173→- Must not touch: `main`, another milestone's worktree, `rust-toolchain.toml` without a decision,
174→  the shared files (§2), the ruleset on `main`.

375→## 5. Architecture
376→
377→Each decision carries its reason. Numbers come from the PRD and `config/observatory.example.toml`
378→unless a reason says otherwise.
379→
380→### 5.1 Crates and interfaces
381→
382→| Crate / app | Responsibility | Public interface | Reason |
383→|---|---|---|---|
384→| `crates/observatory-core` | ingest, model, mapping, store, metrics, control, telemetry; **no UI dependency, sync, no tokio** | `Source` trait, `Event`, `Store`, `Metrics`, `Control`, `Config` | Testable from fixtures alone; every milestone's logic lives here so the UI can be swapped (PRD §12 go/no-go). |
385→| `crates/observatory-cli` | headless `replay`, `inspect`, `attach --watch`, `metrics --csv` over core | `observatory-cli <cmd>` | Rule 2: the first thing that works; rule 5: what CI runs; the validators' oracle for every milestone. |
386→| `apps/observatory-app` | Tauri 2 shell (`src-tauri`) + Leptos CSR UI (`src`) | Tauri commands and events, serde types imported from core | One language, no bindings drift (PRD §12). Commands are the only boundary the UI crosses, so a TypeScript UI could replace it without touching core. |
387→
388→Tauri commands (M1 onward): `open_replay(path)`, `list_sessions()`, `attach(session_id)`,
389→`event_raw(ptr)`, `host_launch(cfg)`, `host_control(cmd)`, `metrics(scope)`, `gate(mission)`,
390→`merge(pr, target)`, `telemetry_status()`. Events from shell to UI: `events_appended(batch)`,
391→`session_discovered`, `stall_flag`, `gate_changed`. Batches flush every 100 ms (reason: well under
392→the 1 s requirement, avoids one render per line).
393→
394→### 5.2 Canonical event and lane mapping
395→
396→`Event`, `ReworkWindow`, `Lane`, `Role`, `EventKind` as in PRD appendix A; `EventKind` has one
397→variant per PRD §7 kind in `CamelCase` plus `Unknown { raw_type }`. `source: SourcePtr::Jsonl {
398→path, byte_offset, byte_len }` is the only thing the store keeps of a raw line (PRD §11.2: the
399→lane is a view). Mapping is a module `mapping::v1` with a `MappingVersion` selected from the Droid
400→version in the session `.settings.json`; unknown Droid versions use the latest mapping and raise a
401→one-line warning (reason: an old capture must keep replaying, rule 18 covers the rest). A mapping
402→version is frozen at M0 and never edited; a later Droid release gets `mapping::v2` and its own
403→fixture. The golden file `fixtures/streams/<capture>.events.json` is the contract of a version.
404→
405→### 5.3 Store schema
406→
407→SQLite via `rusqlite` with the `bundled` feature (reason: core is sync, a desktop index needs no
408→async driver, and bundling removes the system-library dependency from the clean-clone rule).
409→File: `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite` (schema version table, migrations forward-only).
410→
411→| Table | Columns (keys) | Note |
412→|---|---|---|
413→| `sessions` | `id`, `path`, `droid_version`, `tag`, `role`, `parent_id`, `mission_id`, `started_at`, `ended_at` | One row per JSONL file; `tag` confirmed in M0 |
414→| `events` | `id`, `session_id`, `mission_id`, `milestone_id`, `feature_id`, `lane`, `kind`, `raw_type`, `role`, `model`, `at`, `duration_ms`, `path`, `byte_offset`, `byte_len` | Pointer, never payload |
415→| `usage` | `event_id`, `input`, `output`, `cache_read`, `cache_write`, `credits` | From `usage.reported` |
416→| `missions`, `milestones`, `features` | ids, names, `defined_at`, `completed_at`, `state` | Board model |
417→| `rework_windows` | `feature_id`, `opened_by`, `closed_by`, `cause` | PRD §10.2 |
418→| `prs`, `checks`, `attestations`, `reviews` | GitHub ids, state, `observed_at`, `url` | Lane 8 |
419→| `human_actions` | `id`, `kind`, `target`, `at`, `payload_ptr` | Lane 7 |
420→| `prices` | `effective`, `model`, `class`, `per_m`, `source` | Loaded from the dated TOML |
421→| `mapping_versions` | `version`, `droid_version_range`, `frozen_at` | §5.2 |
422→
423→Raw lines are read on demand from `path`+`byte_offset`; if the file moved, the UI says so and
424→shows the pointer (reason: never copy raw lines, PRD §11.3).
425→
426→### 5.4 Ingest adapters behind traits
427→
428→```rust
429→pub trait Source { fn poll(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<RawRecord>>; fn kind(&self) -> SourceKind; }
430→pub trait Forge  { fn pr(&self, branch: &str, target: &str) -> Result<Option<Pr>>;
431→                   fn checks(&self, pr: &Pr) -> Result<Vec<Check>>; fn policy(&self, target: &str) -> Result<MergePolicy>;
432→                   fn merge(&self, pr: &Pr, method: MergeMethod) -> Result<Merged>; /* attestations, reviews */ }
433→```
434→
435→`JsonlSource` (attach; replay = the same source at end of file with a clock the scrubber drives),
436→`RpcSource` (host, M2), `GitSource` (M4), `GitHubSource: Forge` (M4). Reason: one adapter for
437→attach and replay removes a whole class of "works in replay, not live" bugs (D-008); the `Forge`
438→trait is the seam for other forges later (PRD §5 non-goal, §11.2).
439→
440→### 5.5 Config keys with defaults
441→
442→Everything in `config/observatory.example.toml` as committed (`[mission]`, `[ingest]`, `[github]`,
443→`[intervention]`, `[metrics]`, `[telemetry]`), with these additions the mission makes, each with
444→its reason in the file (rule 4):
445→
446→| Key | Default | Reason |
447→|---|---|---|
448→| `[ingest].max_watched_sessions` | 64 | Bounds file handles and tail threads on a laptop; beyond it the newest are watched and the UI says how many are not. |
449→| `[ingest].max_session_file_mb` | 512 | Larger files are indexed but tail reads warn; protects memory on runaway sessions. |
450→| `[ingest].tail_chunk_kb` | 1024 | Read size per tail step; one chunk per poll keeps latency under 1 s at typical mission output rates. |
451→| `[ui].event_batch_ms` | 100 | Shell→UI flush interval (§5.1). |
452→| `[ui].dev_port` | 3141 | `trunk serve` port for the browser host used by validators (§6); chosen outside common dev ranges, confirmed free at planning. |
453→| `[store].path` | `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite` | One index per user; raw lines stay where Droid wrote them. |
454→| `[telemetry].max_milestone_labels` | 8 | 7 named milestones of this mission plus one `overflow` value; bounds the `milestone` label for any observed mission (§5.7). |
455→| `[telemetry].mission_switch_min_interval_min` | 30 | The exported mission changes at most twice an hour, so two missions' series never count as active together (§5.7). |
456→| `[telemetry].buckets.mission_cycle_seconds` | `[3600, 7200, 14400, 28800, 86400, 172800]` | Missions run hours to days. |
457→| `[telemetry].buckets.feature_cycle_seconds` | `[600, 1800, 3600, 7200, 14400]` | Features run minutes to hours. |
458→
459→### 5.6 Metric definitions
460→
461→By reference, not restated: time states PRD §10.1, rework windows §10.2, mission overhead §10.3,
462→cycle/waste/bottleneck/fix loops §10.4, cost §10.5. Closed cause lists used by the engine and the
463→exporter: **waste causes** `waiting_human_question`, `waiting_human_permission`, `waiting_merge`,
464→`waiting_validation`, `rework`, `retry_failure`, `idle_queued`, `idle_unscheduled` (8);
465→**rework causes** `scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate` (4). Mission overhead is a
466→separate line in the app and is not exported (reason: it belongs to no card and D-010 has no label
467→for it). The CSV export has one row per feature with every §10.4 measure and the price-table date.
468→
469→### 5.7 Telemetry series budget (D-010, B-017)
470→
471→Contract: OTLP `http/protobuf` to `https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp`; header
472→value only from the keychain item `droid-observatory/otlp-headers`; resource attributes
473→`service.name=droid-observatory`, `service.version`; labels only from `mission`, `milestone`,
474→`role`, `model`, `cause`; counters and histograms only; one mission exported at a time.
475→
476→| Metric | Instrument | Labels | Cardinality (worst case) | Series |
477→|---|---|---|---|---|
478→| `observatory.mission.cycle_seconds` | histogram, 6 buckets | `mission` | 1 × (6 + `+Inf` + `_sum` + `_count`) | 9 |
479→| `observatory.feature.cycle_seconds` | histogram, 5 buckets | `mission` | 1 × (5 + 3) | 8 |
480→| `observatory.waste_seconds` | counter | `mission`, `milestone`, `cause` | 8 milestones × 8 causes | 64 |
481→| `observatory.rework_windows` | counter | `mission`, `milestone`, `cause` | 8 × 4 | 32 |
482→| `observatory.fix_loops` | counter | `mission`, `milestone` | 8 | 8 |
483→| `observatory.tokens.{input,output,cache_read,cache_write}` | 4 counters | `mission`, `role`, `model` | 3 roles × 4 models = 12 pairs × 4 | 48 |
484→| `observatory.cost_usd` | counter | `mission`, `role`, `model` | 12 | 12 |
485→| `observatory.unknown_events` | counter | `mission` | 1 | 1 |
486→| **Total worst case** | | | | **182** |
487→
488→Expected for this mission (7 milestones, 3 role×model pairs): 9 + 8 + 56 + 28 + 7 + 12 + 3 + 1 =
489→**124**. Both are strictly under 200. Why these shapes: the feature-cycle histogram carries no
490→`milestone` label because a histogram per milestone (7 series each) would cost 56 series for a
491→distribution the app already shows per card; waste and rework keep `milestone` because the budget
492→meter and the waste chart are read per card. Guards: the `milestone` label is bounded by
493→`max_milestone_labels` (the ninth and later milestones of any observed mission export as
494→`milestone="overflow"`); `role` is the closed `Role` enum; `model` beyond four distinct values per
495→mission exports as `model="other"`; the exporter refuses to start if its computed worst case for the
496→configured buckets and limits is not under `[telemetry].max_series`, and the test
497→`exported_series_count_is_under_budget_on_worst_case_labels()` pins the 182. Series of a previous
498→mission stop being written when the export target changes; `mission_switch_min_interval_min` keeps
499→the two sets from overlapping inside Grafana's active-series window. A `service.version` change
500→(release) re-keys the resource once; it is not a steady-state cost. CI telemetry stays deferred
501→(B-002).
502→
503→### 5.8 Runtime limits
504→
505→From §5.5: 64 watched sessions, 512 MB per session file before warnings, 1 MiB tail chunk,
506→100 ms UI batch, 500 ms JSONL poll, 30 s GitHub poll, 15 s metric export, 20 min stall threshold.
507→The UI holds at most the visible window of events; everything else is a store query (reason: a
508→mission can emit tens of thousands of lines; the board must stay at 60 fps on a laptop). The host
509→child process is reaped on window close (M2 test). No network access except GitHub (when a token
510→is present) and the OTLP gateway (when enabled); both are shown in a status bar.
511→
512→### 5.9 Security
513→
514→- Secrets only from the macOS keychain or the environment (rule 4): `droid-observatory/github-token`
515→  or `GITHUB_TOKEN` for lane 8; `droid-observatory/otlp-headers` for telemetry (no environment
516→  fallback in the app, D-010). Never in config, store, logs or the exported telemetry.
517→- Raw JSONL is rendered read-only after the B-006 scrub pass, never uploaded, never copied into the
518→  store (PRD §11.3). Fixtures are committed only after gitleaks and a human read (§3).
519→- The one outward write is the merge (FR-G5): confirmation names PR number and target branch;
520→  the app uses the repository's allowed merge method; the action is a lane-7 event.
521→- Telemetry carries no session id, event id, feature id or free text (D-010); the label allow-list
522→  is enforced in code and by test.
523→
524→## 6. Tests
525→
526→Fixtures are captured streams, named and dated (§3). Local = `make check` in a worktree; MB = the
527→`mission-checks` aggregate on `mission/**`; PR = the `gate` aggregate on the final pull request.
528→
529→| Suite | Covers | Where | Command |
530→|---|---|---|---|
531→| Unit (`#[cfg(test)]` next to code) | model, mapping helpers, time-state engine, windows, cost, label allow-list | local, MB, PR | `cargo test --workspace --all-features` |
532→| Fixture replay (`crates/observatory-core/tests/replay_*.rs`, `mapping.rs`) | each fixture → golden lane events, `unknown events: 0` on frozen captures | local, MB, PR | `make replay-fixtures`; `cargo test -p observatory-core --test mapping` |
533→| Attach latency (`tests/attach_latency.rs`) | harness appends a fixture line by line; event visible to the store within 1 s | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-core --test attach_latency` |
534→| CLI (`crates/observatory-cli/tests/cli.rs`) | exit codes, `unknown events: N` line, `inspect` prints the exact raw line | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-cli` |
535→| Metrics oracle (`tests/oracle.rs`, M5) | engine output vs `reports/reference/*.csv` within tolerance | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-core --test oracle` |
536→| Telemetry budget (M5) | worst-case series count = 182 < 200; labels outside the set rejected | local, MB, PR | part of unit |
537→| UI logic | view-model functions (card position, filters, scrubber) live in core and are unit-tested there; the Leptos layer holds no logic worth a wasm test runner (reason: `wasm-bindgen-test` adds a toolchain step for little coverage) | local, MB, PR | part of unit |
538→| Interactive QA (validators) | board, Details, tray, filters, scrubber in the **browser host** `trunk serve --port 3141` with the fixture opened through the file picker; attach, host, controls and gate in the **Tauri window** (`make app-dev`) with screenshots and the CLI as oracle | per milestone, by the user-testing validator | `make app-dev`; `trunk serve --port 3141` |
539→| Coverage (B-005) | `observatory-core` lines | S: reported; **M0 onward: fail under 80 %**; MB and PR | `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80` |
540→
541→**B-005 settled: 80 % lines on `observatory-core`.** Reason: core holds every piece of logic that
542→can be wrong silently (mapping, time states, cost), so it is where coverage buys correctness;
543→IO adapters that need a live `droid` or GitHub are in core too and cannot all be exercised in CI,
544→which is the 20 % of room. The CLI is thin and covered by its own tests without a threshold; the
545→UI crate is excluded (wasm target, no logic). Enforced from M0 integration because S has too little
546→code for a percentage to mean anything. Raising it is a backlog item with a reason, lowering it is
547→a decision file.
548→
549→## 7. CI
550→
551→Two workflows, one required check (D-003). Measured per run; the wall time of the aggregate is
552→pasted into `reports/ci/<date>-<milestone>.md` at integration (rule 11).
553→
554→**Mission branch** (`mission-branch.yml`, on push and PR to `mission/**`; aggregate
555→`mission-checks`; budget 3 min warm): markdownlint, lychee, actionlint, file size, debt markers,
556→decisions index, gitleaks, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`,
557→`make replay-fixtures`, `cargo deny check`, plus from S: **`cargo machete`** (B-014) and
558→**`cargo llvm-cov` with the §6 threshold** (B-005). Independent jobs in parallel with the
559→rust-cache. Gates integration: the orchestrator waits for green before the next milestone. If the
560→warm time exceeds 3 min after the coverage job joins, coverage moves to the final PR only, by
561→decision file.
562→
563→**B-014 settled: `cargo-machete`, not `cargo-udeps`.** Reason: machete runs on the stable toolchain
564→in seconds; udeps needs nightly, which is a second toolchain to pin and cache for a check that
565→finds a strict superset only in edge cases. Revisit if machete misses a real unused dependency.
566→
567→**Demo gate** (`demo-gate.yml`, M4, on `pull_request` to `demo/base`): one job that fails when the
568→label `demo:red` is present. Required by the `demo-gate` ruleset on `demo/base` only. Never touches
569→`main`.
570→
571→**Final pull request** (`gate.yml`, on PR to `main`; aggregate `gate`, the only check the `main`
572→ruleset requires): everything above plus Semgrep (SARIF to code scanning), Trivy filesystem scan on
573→`Cargo.lock` (HIGH, CRITICAL), Checkov on the workflows, SBOM (`syft`), the macOS Tauri bundle
574→(`bundle.yml`) with build provenance (`attest-build-provenance`) and cosign signatures, Trivy
575→results and SBOM attached as artifacts. It never deploys. `release.yml` on `v*` tags pushed by the
576→human to a commit on `main` reuses `bundle.yml` and checks the workspace version against the tag
577→(B-016, D-009).
578→
579→## 8. Deliverables

581→Grown at every integration, never written at the end (rule 16).

## ai/RULES.md
1→# Rules
2→
3→The rules this project inherits, adapted for a build run as a Factory Mission (orchestrator, workers, validators) with the human as owner. Derived from the artstudio set (14-oct-2026); rules that only made sense for a hand-run team are struck, not deleted, so the decision is visible.
4→
5→1. **Tests before code.** No production code without a failing test that asks for it. Workers write the test first and commit it red; validators check that the red run exists in the log. Tests are the contract between the spec and the build.
6→2. **A walking skeleton first.** The thinnest end-to-end slice (core crate, canonical event model, `observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is on the mission branch before any milestone deepens its area, so every integration is checked by real acceptance tests.
7→3. **Versions verified, latest stable.** Every crate, tool and image is pinned to a version checked against the official source on the day it is added; the spec's version table says when.
8→4. **No secrets, no magic values.** Credentials only from the OS keychain or the environment, never in the repo, the store or the logs; every number (poll interval, stall threshold, price) comes from configuration with a stated default and a reason in the spec.
9→5. **Everything from a clean clone.** `cargo test`, `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay <fixture>` and the app build work on a machine that has only the Rust toolchain and the Tauri prerequisites; the README's commands are the ones CI runs.
10→6. **CI is a gate, not infrastructure.** Light checks on the mission branch: `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`, the replay fixtures, `cargo deny` (advisories and licences), gitleaks. The full attested run on the one pull request into `main`: everything above plus Semgrep (SAST), Trivy filesystem scan on `Cargo.lock`, Checkov on the workflows themselves, an SBOM (`syft` or `cargo-sbom`), the Tauri bundle built on macOS, build provenance with `actions/attest-build-provenance`, cosign-signed artifacts, with the Trivy results and the SBOM attached to the release. It never deploys.
11→7. **Counts come off the tool.** Test counts, timings, token usage and scan results are pasted from the run that produced them, never estimated.
12→8. **The spec is as-built.** When the code and the spec disagree at the end of a milestone, the spec is updated in the same integration, with the reason in `docs/decisions/`.
13→9. **Deviations are the human's to approve.** The orchestrator proposes, with reason and cost, and waits.
14→10. **Honest time.** The README states the real time and usage spent per milestone; what was left out is listed, not hidden.
15→11. **CI under three minutes warm on the mission branch.** Independent jobs in parallel, cargo and tool caches, prebuilt actions; the heavy stage only on the final pull request. Measured per run and reported.
16→12. **Git forward only, one PR per mission.** Never amend, reset, rebase or stash; a mistake is fixed by a new commit. Milestones live in worktrees and are integrated into `mission/<name>`; nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. A milestone is never shippable; the mission is.
17→13. **One file per decision, no shared files across worktrees.** `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` (what, why, alternatives, consequences); the index is generated. Two worktrees never edit the same file; the living spec sections are written by the orchestrator on the mission branch at integration time.
18→14. **Review fixes what blocks.** Blocking and security findings are fixed in the milestone, once; everything else goes to `BACKLOG.md` with its reason. A review never starts a second round for style.
19→15. **Nothing reaches an agent mid-task.** Decisions are settled before a milestone starts; what comes up later waits for the next milestone or goes to the backlog. The human messages the mission only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up.
20→16. **Deliverables grow with the work.** README, decisions, backlog, build-log and the session log start with the skeleton and are extended at every integration, never written at the end.
21→17. **Everything is logged.** Hooks record every tool call to `build-log/`; every session transcript is linked from the session log; usage per model and per milestone is recorded. The build of the observatory is itself a dataset for the observatory.
22→18. **Unknown is surfaced, never dropped.** An event the mapper does not recognise is counted and shown; a milestone that adds a source ends with zero unknown events on its capture.
23→19. **Models per role are declared.** Orchestrator, worker and validator models are named in the spec and in the mission command; a change of model is a decision file.
24→
25→Struck from the artstudio set: *tester, coder and reviewer as separate agents per team* (the Mission's workers and validators take those roles; if the validators prove weaker, custom sub-droids bring the split back, as a decision); *the 90-minute box* (replaced by usage budgets per milestone).

1→# D-010: Telemetry contract for the Grafana Cloud stack
2→
3→**Date:** 2026-10-22
4→**Status:** accepted (owner-provided contract; code in the telemetry milestone)
5→
6→## Context
7→
8→D-004 chose Grafana Cloud over OTLP and sketched metric names with a wide attribute list
9→(`feature`, `session`, `class`, `unit`, `price_table`, a gauge for active agents). The owner
10→has provisioned the stack and set the operating constraints below. Cardinality on Grafana
11→Cloud is billed per active series, so the attribute set is the contract that matters.
12→
13→## Decision
14→
15→- **Transport:** OTLP over HTTP (`http/protobuf`) to
16→  `https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp` (`/v1/metrics`, `/v1/traces`,
17→  `/v1/logs`). The endpoint is not a secret and lives in `config/observatory.example.toml`.
18→- **Credential:** the full `Authorization=Basic …` header value is read at runtime from the
19→  macOS keychain item with service `droid-observatory/otlp-headers` and account = the
20→  current user. It is never written to config, the store or logs. If the item is missing,
21→  telemetry stays off and the UI says so (a visible "telemetry: off, no keychain item"
22→  state, not a silent failure). The environment variable `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` is
23→  for CI only (B-002); the app does not read it.
24→- **Resource attributes:** `service.name=droid-observatory` and `service.version` (the
25→  crate version). Nothing else. D-004's `deployment.environment` and `service.namespace`
26→  are dropped.
27→- **Metric attributes (labels):** only from the set `mission`, `milestone`, `role`,
28→  `model`, `cause`. Never a session id, event id, feature id or free text. Anything
29→  that varied by `class`, `unit` or `status` in D-004 becomes part of the metric name
30→  (for example `observatory.tokens.input`, `observatory.cost_usd`) or is not exported.
31→- **Instruments:** counters and histograms only. No per-event gauges;
32→  `observatory.active_agents` is not exported (it stays an in-app view).
33→- **Series budget:** the spec states the exact metric set and the number of active series
34→  the app adds, computed from the label cardinalities, and keeps it **under 200**. The
35→  arithmetic is the spec's (B-017); the shape it must fit is: one mission exporting at a
36→  time, up to 6 milestones, 3 roles, up to 4 models, a closed list of waste causes, and a
37→  histogram costs one series per bucket plus `_sum` and `_count`, so explicit bucket
38→  boundaries are part of the contract.
39→
40→## Alternatives
41→
42→- Keep D-004's attribute list and rely on Grafana's adaptive metrics to aggregate: pays for
43→  the series first, then hides them; rejected.
44→- Export per-feature series: `feature` would be the largest cardinality by far and is
45→  already visible in the app; rejected by the owner.
46→- Read the header from the environment as a fallback in the app: one more place a secret can
47→  leak into a shell history or a log; rejected by the owner.
48→
49→## Consequences
50→
51→- D-004 stays accepted for the choice of backend and the two kinds of telemetry; its
52→  attribute list, resource attributes and the gauge are superseded here.
53→- `config/observatory.example.toml` `[telemetry]` carries the endpoint, the keychain
54→  service name, the allowed label set, the series budget and the revised metric names.
55→- PRD v0.5 §11.4 states the contract. `.env.example` marks the OTLP variables CI-only.
56→- B-017: the spec session computes the series count and names the histogram buckets.

## ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md
1→# PRD: droid-observatory
2→
3→| Field | Value |
4→|---|---|
5→| Status | Draft v0.5 for review |
6→| Date | 2026-10-22 |
7→| Owner | dct |
8→| Author | Droid (ideation session, see `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md`) |
9→| Changes from v0.1 to v0.4 | See Appendix C |
10→
11→---
12→
13→## 1. Summary
14→
15→droid-observatory is a Rust desktop application that shows how a Factory Mission moves through the engineering build cycle. It renders the mission as a board whose lanes are the orchestrated states of a mission, from the human's intent through orchestration, building, validation, integration, the human gate, and the outside ecosystem (PR, CI, deploy). Alongside the flow it measures what the flow costs: cycle time, waste by cause, tokens and money per sub-droid and per model.
16→
17→The observatory attaches to missions started from any terminal on this machine (it watches `~/.factory/sessions/` and tails each new session file as it grows), replays finished ones from the same files, and can also host a mission itself (it spawns `droid exec --mission` and consumes the JSON-RPC event stream, which adds the control channel). Attach is the primary live mode; hosting is the secondary path. It never copies the event data into a second source of truth: every lane entry is a view over the raw JSONL line it came from.
18→
19→A mission is not complete when the workers stop. It is complete when the gate is green and the merge has happened.
20→
21→## 2. Delivery model
22→
23→This section defines the units the board shows. Everything else follows from it.
24→
25→- **A mission is a business feature: the unit that ships.** For this project, v1 of the observatory. A mission ends in **one PR into `main`**, outcome-sized, with the evidence attached. The full attested CI runs on that PR; CD runs from `main`.
26→- **Milestones are internal iterations**, not shippable. Each milestone runs in its own worktree and is integrated into a **`mission/<name>` branch**, the mission's interface to `main`. Fast checks (tests, lint, the gate command) run on that branch to keep it healthy. Nothing on it is shippable or pretends to be.
27→- **The mission branch is short-lived by construction.** It dies at the merge. That is what keeps it from becoming a long-lived `dev` branch.
28→- **Features** are the orchestrator's work items inside a milestone. Workers build them, validators judge them, and metrics are computed at feature granularity, then rolled up to the milestone and the mission.
29→- **The fix loop after CI red reopens the mission on its branch.** It does not open a new PR. The same PR goes green or stays red.
30→
31→On the board: **cards are milestones**; the gate group in lane 8 is the mission's one PR; lane 6 is integration into `mission/<name>`; lane 8 is the PR.
32→
33→**Models per role** (decision D-006; `ai/RULES.md` rule 19): orchestrator `claude-fable-5.1`, workers `claude-sonnet-5-5`, validators `claude-opus-5-5`. Reasoning effort per role is declared in the spec. A change of model is a decision file.
34→
35→The orchestrator catalog ID spelling was corrected on 2026-10-22 (D-006); Appendix C retains the historical spelling.
36→
37→## 3. Problem
38→
39→Mission Control (CLI and Factory App) shows progress, workers, and a log. It does not show:
40→
41→- the mission's full life, including what happens after the workers stop (PR, CI, attestations, deploy, red builds that need a fix);
42→- where time goes: active work versus waiting on a human, waiting on validation, waiting on merge, rework after a blocking finding, retries and conflicts;
43→- what each role and model consumed, so that model and reasoning-effort choices can be compared with real numbers;
44→- a single place to act when the mission needs a human: approve, answer, redirect, merge.
45→
46→Running missions without that view means managing agents blind on the two dimensions that matter most for an engineering organization: flow and cost.
47→
48→## 4. Goals
49→
50→1. Show every milestone of a mission across the nine lanes defined in section 7, live and in replay, with features visible inside each card.
51→2. Show per card: validation state (red/green), current agent, gate state, and a Details view with review notes, validation criteria, commits, and raw event links.
52→3. Let the human act from the board: pause/resume the orchestrator, send instructions, answer escalations, approve, mark a feature complete or skipped, and merge the PR when policy says a human merges.
53→4. Measure cycle time, waste by cause, mission overhead, and bottlenecks per feature, per milestone, per role, and per mission.
54→5. Measure cost: tokens per sub-droid, converted to Factory Standard Credits when the stream exposes them, otherwise money via a dated price table that every displayed cost references.
55→6. Treat CI red on the mission PR as a counted rework loop: reopen the mission on its branch, loop the affected card back into the Workers lane, keep the same PR.
56→
57→## 5. Non-goals (v1)
58→
59→- Replacing Mission Control for planning. The observatory starts after a plan exists (it may launch the mission, but the plan conversation stays in Droid).
60→- Multi-user or server deployment. v1 is a single-user desktop app reading local data and the user's own GitHub access.
61→- Writing to Factory's hosted API beyond what the local `droid` process already does.
62→- Editing code or reviewing diffs inside the app. It links out to the worktree, commit, or PR.
63→- Supporting CI systems other than GitHub Actions in v1 (adapter boundary is defined so others can follow).
64→
65→## 6. Users
66→
67→**Mission owner (primary).** The engineer acting as project manager of agents. Wants to see progress, act when needed, and know what the mission cost in time and money.
68→
69→**Reviewer / gatekeeper.** Opens the Details view, reads scrutiny findings and QA results, watches the outcome video, and merges or sends back.
70→
71→**Engineering lead (reader).** Compares missions and models over time: cycle time, waste, cost per feature. Does not intervene.
72→
73→## 7. Lanes
74→
75→The board has nine lanes. Lanes 1–6 are fed by the mission stream, 7–8 by GitHub and human actions, 9 by session metadata. Each event carries `session_id`, `role`, `model`, `timestamp`, `duration`, and a pointer to its raw JSONL line.
76→
77→| # | Lane | What it holds | Source | Event kinds |
78→|---|---|---|---|---|
79→| 1 | **Intent** | Mission prompt, spec, acceptance criteria; later human re-prompts | stream (user ↔ orchestrator), mission file | `intent.created`, `intent.amended`, `question.asked` (orchestrator → human), `intent.answered`, `spec.versioned` |
80→| 2 | **Orchestrator** | Plan, feature breakdown, milestones, task assignment, replans | stream (orchestrator session) | `plan.created`, `feature.defined`, `milestone.defined`, `task.assigned`, `task.skipped`, `plan.revised`, `escalation.raised`, `milestone.completed`, `mission.paused`, `mission.resumed`, `mission.completed`, `context.compacted` |
81→| 3 | **Workers** | One sub-lane per worker (or per feature when the mission names them) | stream (worker child sessions) | `subagent.spawned`, `task.started`, `file.touched`, `tests.run`, `commit.created`, `task.done`, `subagent.finished`, `tool.error`, `permission.requested`, `permission.granted`, `permission.denied`, `hook.blocked`, `usage.reported`, `model.changed` |
82→| 4 | **Validators, scrutiny** | Review findings, blocking vs non-blocking, re-work requested and resolved | stream (scrutiny validator sessions) | `finding.blocking`, `finding.non_blocking`, `rework.requested`, `rework.resolved`, `scrutiny.passed` |
83→| 5 | **Validators, user testing** | QA runs against the built thing, scenario results | stream (user-testing validator sessions) | `qa.scenario.passed`, `qa.scenario.failed`, `qa.evidence` (screenshot, video) |
84→| 6 | **Integration** | Worktree merges into `mission/<name>`, conflicts, fast checks. Wording is "integrated in mission", never "merged" | stream (orchestrator/worker git activity) | `integration.merged`, `integration.conflict`, `integration.conflict_resolved`, `gate_command.run`, `gate_command.passed`, `gate_command.failed` |
85→| 7 | **Human** | Approvals, answers to escalations, review of the outcome (the video), the merge of the PR | app actions, stream attention events | `approval.requested`, `approval.given`, `question.answered`, `review.outcome`, `pr.merged_by_human` |
86→| 8 | **Outside** | The mission PR into `main`: opened, reviews, checks, attestations, merge, deploys. Empty for the observatory itself until its final PR | GitHub adapter | `pr.opened`, `pr.review_requested`, `check.started`, `check.passed`, `check.failed`, `check.required_missing`, `ruleset.blocked`, `attestation.recorded`, `attestation.verified`, `pr.merged_by_policy`, `deploy.completed` |
87→| 9 | **Time, Waste, Cost and models** | Tokens and usage per role, which model did what; budget meter; elapsed, stuck, and wasted time; mission overhead | derived from all lanes + session metadata | computed, not evented |
88→

95→## 8. Board model
96→
97→**Card = one milestone.** The milestone is the spec phase: the orchestrator plans it, workers build its features in a worktree, validators judge it, and it integrates into `mission/<name>`. Each card lists its features with their individual state, and metrics roll up feature → milestone → mission.
98→
99→A card moves left to right. Its position is the lane where its most recent open activity is. The Details view shows the full history across lanes.
100→
101→**Gate group.** Lane 8 holds one group per mission: the mission PR. All cards of the mission share that gate state; the badge sits on the group. Until the PR exists, lane 8 shows the mission branch with its fast-check status as a pre-gate placeholder.
102→
103→**Fix loop.** When CI goes red on the mission PR, the observatory reopens the mission on `mission/<name>` with a cycle tagged `fix` on the milestone(s) whose features the fix touches. Those cards are drawn with a loop arrow back into lane 3. The PR stays the same. The loop is counted as rework in lane 9.
104→
105→**Mission completion.** Mission state is `complete` only when the PR is merged with CI green. Until then it is `planning`, `building`, `validating`, `at gate`, or `fixing`.

111→│ M2  Host                                    [Details]│
112→│ features 4/6 done · worktree wt/m2 · mission/obs-v1  │
113→│ ● validation: RED (1 blocking)  ◆ branch: fast checks ✓│
114→│ now: worker-3 (claude-sonnet-5-5) on F-014 · 00:14:22 │
115→│ cycle 2h 10m · waste 38m (rework 22m, human 16m)      │
116→│ 412k tok · $1.84 (prices 2026-10-22)                  │
117→└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

121→│ ◆ gate: HUMAN REQUIRED · checks 7/7 ✓ · attested ✓     │
122→│ cards: M0 M1 M2 M3 M4 M5                      [Merge]  │
123→└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

203→## 10. Metric definitions
204→
205→### 10.1 Time states
206→
207→Each feature, at every instant, is in exactly one time state:
208→
209→| State | Definition |
210→|---|---|
211→| **Active** | A worker, validator, or orchestrator is doing something for the feature: tool call in flight or model generating. |
212→| **Waiting on human** | A question or approval is open and nobody is acting (lane 7 open, lanes 2–6 idle for this feature). Sub-causes: *question*, *permission*, *waiting on merge* (checks green, policy requires a human, nobody has merged). |
213→| **Waiting on validation** | Work is done, validator not started. |
214→| **Retry and failure** | Time in tool errors, `hook.blocked`, re-runs of the same command, and conflict resolution. |
215→| **Idle, queued** | Feature is planned and ready but blocked behind another feature (WIP limit, dependency, no free worker). A bottleneck signal. |
216→| **Idle, unscheduled** | Feature exists but nothing is scheduled and nothing is blocking it. Not a bottleneck signal. |
217→
218→Rework is not a separate time state. It is a window (10.2) that overlays active, retry, and waiting time.
219→
220→### 10.2 Rework windows
221→
222→A **rework window** opens at a blocking signal and closes at its resolution event, per signal:
223→
224→| Opens | Closes |
225→|---|---|
226→| `finding.blocking` | `rework.resolved` |
227→| `qa.scenario.failed` | `qa.scenario.passed` for the same scenario |
228→| `integration.conflict` | `integration.conflict_resolved` |
229→| `check.failed` (mission PR) | `check.passed` for the same check |
230→
231→Overlapping windows on the same feature merge into one. A window with no closing event stays open until mission end and is reported as unresolved.
232→
233→- **Rework time** = active time inside rework windows.
234→- **First-pass active time** = active time outside any rework window.
235→
236→This bounds rework so that legitimate new work after a fix is not counted as waste.
237→
238→### 10.3 Mission overhead
239→
240→Orchestrator time before the first `feature.defined`, replanning time not attributable to one feature, and `context.compacted` recovery belong to no card. They are reported as **mission overhead**, a separate line in lane 9, never apportioned silently. An optional explicit apportionment (equal split across features) can be switched on for comparisons and is labeled as such.
241→
242→### 10.4 Derived measures
243→
244→- **Cycle time** (feature) = `feature.defined` → feature's last `task.done` with validation green and integrated. **Cycle time** (milestone) = `milestone.defined` → `milestone.completed`. **Cycle time** (mission) = `intent.created` → `pr.merged` (human or policy) with CI green. Stage cycle times are computed per lane.
245→- **Waste** = total elapsed − first-pass active time, split by cause: waiting on human (question, permission, merge), waiting on validation, rework, retry and failure, idle queued, idle unscheduled. Mission overhead is reported next to waste, not inside it. Reported per feature, per milestone, and per role.
246→- **Bottleneck** = lane or role with the highest sum of waiting plus queued time across features in the window, and the lane with the highest WIP relative to its throughput.
247→- **Fix loops** = count of `fix` cycles per milestone and per mission.
248→
249→### 10.5 Cost
250→
251→- Token counts are taken from `usage.reported` events per session (input, output, cache read, cache write when available).
252→- If the stream reports Factory Standard Credits, credits are the primary unit.
253→- Otherwise cost = Σ tokens × price per model and token class, from the **price table**: a dated config file (`~/.droid-observatory/prices/<YYYY-MM-DD>.toml`). The board always shows the date of the table it used, and a mission keeps the table it started with unless the user re-prices it explicitly.
254→- Cost is shown next to waste so that a slow, cheap model and a fast, expensive one can be compared on the same panel.

328→
329→- GitHub token and Factory credentials stay in the OS keychain (Tauri keyring plugin). Never written to the store or logs.

333→### 11.4 Telemetry export (Grafana Cloud)
334→
335→Two kinds of telemetry leave the app, both over OpenTelemetry OTLP (`http/protobuf`) to a Grafana Cloud stack, both off by default so the app works fully offline (decision D-004):
336→
337→- **App telemetry**: `tracing` spans for ingest, mapping, metrics, and control; errors as span events.
338→- **Mission metrics**: the lane-9 series, so the budget meter and waste can be charted and alerted on outside the desktop window. 342→## 12. Technology options and recommendation
343→
344→Constraint: Rust. Preference: Tauri 2. Needs: data-dense board, live updates, charts, markdown and video rendering in Details, long-lived subprocess management, SQLite.
345→
346→| Option | Pros | Cons |
347→|---|---|---|
348→| **A. Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust, CSR via Trunk)** | Single language; shared serde types between core and UI with no bindings; fine-grained reactivity suits a live board; webview gives markdown, video, CSS layout for free. | Charting ecosystem thinner than JS; WASM/Trunk toolchain adds build steps; smaller community. **Droids have far less Leptos in their training than React or Svelte**, so worker rework on UI tasks is likely higher. **The WASM/Trunk toolchain inside a Mission is a new failure mode** (toolchain install, target, dev server) that validators may struggle to diagnose. |
349→| B. Tauri 2 + Dioxus | Same single-language benefit; React-like ergonomics; growing fast. | Dioxus also ships its own desktop renderer, which blurs the "why Tauri" story; same training-data and toolchain concerns as A. |
350→| C. Tauri 2 + TypeScript (Svelte or React) | Richest charting and UI libraries; fastest to a polished UI; best-known stack for Droids. | Two languages; types must be generated (ts-rs/specta) and kept in sync; the user's stated preference is Rust. |
351→| D. iced (native) | Pure Rust, no webview, small binary, Elm architecture fits an event-driven board. | Markdown, video, and rich text are weak; complex layouts cost more effort; no Tauri plugin ecosystem (keyring, updater, tray). |
352→| E. egui (native, immediate mode) | Trivial live updates and plots (egui_plot); excellent for dashboards. | Looks like a tool, not an app; text-heavy Details view (review notes, markdown) is awkward; accessibility and theming limited. |
353→
354→**Recommendation: Option A, Tauri 2 + Leptos, with M1 as an explicit go/no-go.**
355→
356→Reasoning: the hard part of this product is `observatory-core` (ingest, mapping, metrics), not the UI. Keeping the UI in Rust means the metric types, lane mapping, and event model are used directly in the view with no translation layer, which is where drift and bugs would otherwise appear. The webview covers the rich-content needs (markdown findings, QA video, PR rendering) that native options handle poorly. Charting is the one real gap; lane 9 needs stacked bars and timelines, achievable as SVG from Leptos signals, with a JS chart library as a documented escape hatch.
357→
358→**Go/no-go criterion (evaluated at M1 completion):** the board renders the M0 replay (all nine lanes, cards positioned correctly, Details timeline open) with **at most 3 worker sessions of rework** after the first scrutiny pass, and the Trunk/WASM build succeeds from a clean checkout with the documented command. If either fails, switch to Option C for M2 onward, keeping `observatory-core` unchanged; the Tauri command boundary is designed to make that swap possible. (Threshold of 3 agreed 2026-10-22; may be adjusted at planning time.)

## docs/decisions/D-003-ci-two-workflows-one-check.md
1→# D-003: Two workflows, one required check, jobs that activate with the code
2→
3→**Date:** 2026-10-22
4→**Status:** accepted
5→
6→## Context
7→
8→RULES.md rule 6 splits CI into light checks on the mission branch (under three minutes
9→warm) and a full attested run on the one PR into `main`. The `main` ruleset must name
10→required checks before any code exists, and a required check that never reports hangs the
11→final PR.
12→
13→## Decision
14→
15→- `mission-branch.yml` (on `mission/**`, also `workflow_call`): docs, links, workflows,
16→  secrets, rust, deny. Aggregate job **`mission-checks`**.
17→- `gate.yml` (on PRs to `main`): reuses the light workflow, adds Semgrep, Trivy fs, Checkov
18→  on the workflows, SBOM (syft), macOS Tauri bundle with `attest-build-provenance` and
19→  cosign keyless signatures. Aggregate job **`gate`**, the only check the ruleset requires.
20→- Aggregate jobs run `if: always()` and fail on any `failure`/`cancelled` in `needs`;
21→  skipped jobs count as not applicable. New jobs are added to `needs`, never to the ruleset.
22→- Rust, fixtures and Tauri jobs are gated by a `detect` job probing for `Cargo.toml`,
23→  `fixtures/streams/*.jsonl`, and `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`.
24→- Every action is pinned to a commit digest with a version comment; Renovate keeps them
25→  current (D-005). Versions verified against GitHub releases on 2026-10-22.
26→- Workflows call `make` targets so README commands and CI commands are the same thing.
27→
28→## Alternatives
29→
30→Listing each job as a required check: brittle, breaks when jobs are renamed or skipped.
31→Separate workflows per tool: more files, no shared `detect`.
32→
33→## Consequences
34→
35→The ruleset (D-007) requires exactly `gate`. The mission must keep the probed paths.
36→
## docs/decisions/D-008-attach-primary-live-mode.md
1→# D-008: Attach is the primary live mode
2→
3→**Date:** 2026-10-22
4→**Status:** accepted
5→
6→## Context
7→
8→Missions are started from the terminal in practice (`droid exec --mission ...` in a
9→project's directory). Every session, including the child sessions of workers and
10→validators, is written as it runs to `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/<id>.jsonl`. PRD v0.3
11→treated hosting (the app spawns `droid exec`) as the live mode and attach as an afterthought,
12→which made a launch screen a prerequisite for watching anything live (M2) and left the
13→dogfooding statement ("from M1 onward") without a mechanism.
14→
15→## Decision
16→
17→Attach is the primary live mode. The observatory watches `~/.factory/sessions/` with a
18→filesystem notifier, detects any new session JSONL, tails it as it grows and renders it
19→within 1 s, named by its `--tag` or session id. Replay is attach at end-of-file: one adapter
20→(`jsonl_watch` + `jsonl_tail`), one code path. Hosting remains as the secondary path and the
21→only mode with a control channel (pause, message, answer over the JSON-RPC input stream).
22→
23→Milestones: attach moves into M1 with replay; M1 acceptance adds "start a mission in a
24→terminal, see its events on the board within 1 s". M2 becomes hosting only. The agent panel
25→and the `model.changed` / `context.compacted` markers move to M1 because they are read-only
26→views over the same events. PRD v0.4, §1, §9.7, §11.1, §11.2, §13, §14, §15.
27→
28→## Alternatives
29→
30→- Host first (v0.3): every observed mission must be launched from the app; nothing can be
31→  watched until the launch screen, process management and RPC plumbing exist.
32→- Attach by explicit file pick only, no watcher: works, but the user has to find the session
33→  id for each mission and misses child sessions.
34→
35→## Consequences
36→
37→- Dogfooding starts the moment M1 lands: M2–M5 of the mission that builds the observatory

## docs/decisions/D-009-release-tag-on-main.md
1→# D-009: Releases are tags on main, built by the gate's bundle workflow
2→
3→**Date:** 2026-10-22
4→**Status:** accepted
5→
6→## Context
7→
8→A mission ends in one PR into `main` (D-001). The gate on that PR already builds the
9→macOS bundle with provenance and a cosign signature (D-003). There was no step that turned
10→a merged mission into something a user can download, and no release notes.
11→
12→## Decision
13→
14→- A release is a semver tag `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` pushed by the human to a commit on
15→  `main`, after the mission PR merges. Tags are not pushed by agents.
16→- `.github/workflows/release.yml` verifies the tag is on `main` and is semver, builds the
17→  bundle through the same reusable `bundle.yml` the gate uses, and creates the GitHub
18→  release with `gh release create --generate-notes`.
19→- Release notes come from GitHub's generator configured in `.github/release.yml`: PRs
20→  grouped by this repository's labels (`type:feature`, `type:bug` and `fix-cycle`,
21→  `type:security`, `type:decision`, `area:deps`, other). The PR title is the note; write it
22→  for the reader.
23→- No deployment, update server or package registry. The release page is the distribution.
24→
25→## Alternatives
26→
27→- `release-plz` or `cargo-release`: version bumps and changelogs from commits; too much
28→  machinery for one PR per mission, and it would need `Cargo.toml` to exist.
29→- `git-cliff` (B-004 as first written): a second notes format next to GitHub's; dropped.
30→- Release on every merge to `main`: a mission PR is already the unit; the human decides
31→  when a merge is a release.
32→
33→## Consequences
34→
35→- `gate.yml` and `release.yml` share `bundle.yml`; a change to how the bundle is built lands
36→  once. The gate's `bundle` job keeps its name, so the ruleset is unchanged.
37→- Until the Tauri app exists, a tag produces a release with notes and no assets.
38→- Version source of truth, once code exists: `Cargo.toml` workspace version, equal to the
39→  tag without `v`. The release workflow does not check this yet; add the check with the
40→  skeleton (TODO is in `BACKLOG.md` as B-016).
